transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-10-14 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Nimbus PM), Jordan Lee (Nimbus ML Eng), Markus Voss (Nimbus CTO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood and Nimbus reviewed pilot cost/unit economics. Key topics: tokens/sec/$ calculations, cache hit savings, batching tradeoffs, 4-bit quantized model performance, and whether to move a subset to dedicated capacity. Action items include running a larger sample, sharing CSVs and scheduling a canary deploy. Nimbus highlighted concerns about latency spikes during cart-peek flows and data security (SSO, audit logs).

Topics:
- tokens/sec/$ and how to interpret the pilot numbers
- prefix/KV cache configuraton & hit rate impact
- batching size impact on P95 latency
- dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs and fallback policies
- next steps and benchmarks

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): okay everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll go quick, agenda is econ playback from last week, caching numbers, and then tuning plays, and then action items. sound good?
[00:06] Priya (Nimbus): yes thanks Alex, we only have about 45 mins so appreciate the focus.
[00:12] Samir (SE): quick note, i've got the initial 2.5k sample run results here, there are a few noisy outliers but the overall tokens per dollar numbers look promising, we'll walk through.
[00:20] Jordan (Nimbus): before you get into it, can you remind us how you calculate tokens/sec/$? last week the slide had a small footnote and i want to make sure we compare apples to apples.
[00:28] Samir (SE): yeah, so tokens/sec/$ is basically throughput (tokens per second) divided by cost per second of the configuration. in our sample we used model: redwood-elerian-3b-quantized (4-bit), batch target 8, and enabled prefix cache with a 40% hit rate observed. so tokens/sec was about 1,120 and cost was $0.083/sec which yields around 13.5 tokens/sec/$. again noisy but ballpark.
[00:45] Markus (Nimbus): 13.5 tokens per dollar, okay, how does that change if the cache hit rate drops? our cart-peek flows vary a lot by user.
[00:52] Samir (SE): good question, with cache hit rate at 20% tokens/sec/$ drops to ~9.2, that's because we are skipping KV cache benefits and some prefix reuse. note our 'KV cache' is sometimes transcribed as 'K V cash' in the logs so ignore that typo. 
[01:10] Priya (Nimbus): and batching? if we bump batch from 8 to 16 what's the impact on latency p95? i'm worried about checkout latency.
[01:18] Samir (SE): bumping to 16 improves tokens/sec/$ to about 18.7 in steady-state but p95 latency grew from 210ms to 360ms on our test rig. also the throughput gains become less predictable under spiky traffic because of batching wait windows. so there's a tradeoff.
[01:34] Jordan (Nimbus): are those numbers on hosted or dedicated instances?
[01:38] Samir (SE): these were on hosted with the provisioned pool we have for the pilot. we also tested a dedicated r12 pool for a short run — dedicated lowered p95 by ~30ms at batch 8 and increased stability, but cost per second was slightly higher which muted tokens/sec/$.
[01:55] Markus (Nimbus): so dedicated is more stable but cost is up, which reduces tokens per dollar. curious, any model quantization impacts? we saw some fuzz on output with 4-bit last time.
[02:04] Samir (SE): yes, 4-bit quant gives ~1.4x throughput vs 8-bit on this arch, cost lower, but you will see occasional degeneration on long-form completions. for the short cart suggestion flows it's fine. there was a transcription note — sometimes 'quantizaton' spelled without the i in our auto-notes.
[02:20] Alex (AE): quick interjection, Nimbus, your success criteria said 95th percentile latency under 350ms for checkout. do we still hold that as a hard req?
[02:28] Priya (Nimbus): yes that's non-negotiable for checkout. for recommendation surfaces we can accept up to 500ms.
[02:33] Alex (AE): ok good, that's helpful. we'll tune for checkout route separately.
[02:38] Samir (SE): specifically, we suggest keeping batch target 8 for checkout route and enable aggressive prefix caching TTL of 60s to maximize reuse; that gave us effective cache hit rate around 36% in a synthetic session test.
[02:52] Jordan (Nimbus): how do you measure cache hit rate? is that on request-level or token-level?
[02:56] Samir (SE): token-level; we report prefix bytes and KV hits per request in the CSV. in the sample the token-level hit was 36% but request-level hit was only 20% because some requests were short and didn't benefit.
[03:09] Priya (Nimbus): ok makes sense. another question: security and audit logs — Markus, do you want to raise anything?
[03:14] Markus (Nimbus): yes, we need to verify audit log retention for private deployment, and SSO / SAML integration. we also want to see proof of SOC2 type 2 reports.
[03:22] Alex (AE): yes, we'll send the security pack and SOC2 link after the call. link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 (note: placeholder in transcript). also we'll include the private deployment checklist if you want to evaluate VPC.
[03:36] Priya (Nimbus): great. back to econ: i see line items in your spreadsheet for token cost and for infra amortization. can you explain infra amortization?
[03:44] Samir (SE): sure — infra amortization is the per-second cost for reserved GPU time amortized over utilization. in dedicated it's more visible since you commit to nodes. in hosted we show usethe per-second spot/commit blended price. that was in the sheet labeled "infra_amort" which sometimes got truncated in the export.
[04:00] Jordan (Nimbus): the sample has a few outliers where latency shot to 1.6s, what caused that?
[04:05] Samir (SE): we dug in, those were cold KV cache misses during a background model swap on the node; we also saw a small garbage collection pause in the runtime during that window. we'll add tracing to catch that.
[04:14] Alex (AE): action item: Samir will run a 10k sample with tracing enabled and share raw CSV + config. will also flag any node-level events.
[04:23] Priya (Nimbus): will you also include the tokens/sec/$ calculation per-route, not just aggregate? we need per-route economics to decide what to move to dedicated.
[04:30] Samir (SE): yep, will split by route (checkout, recs, post-purchase chat).
[04:34] Markus (Nimbus): one more thing — SLA/uptime. if we go to dedicated, what's the uptime SLA and fallback if nodes fail?
[04:39] Alex (AE): Dedicated comes with an SLA; also we can configure automatic fallback to hosted variants (lower capacity) for short windows. the routing policy can be region-based and priority-based. we'll include that in the follow up doc.
[04:52] Jordan (Nimbus): curious about caching eviction policy — you mentioned TTL 60s but what about size-based eviction? we have long sessions with many variants.
[04:58] Samir (SE): right now pilot used LRU with a per-host TTL + size threshold. for Nimbus we can tune threshold and also pin certain prompt prefixes to cache. pinning increases memory use but boosts hit rate for priority routes.
[05:12] Priya (Nimbus): any rough numbers for pinning?
[05:15] Samir (SE): pinning top 200 prefixes improved hit rate to ~52% in a synthetic run but increased memory by ~18% per GPU.
[05:24] Alex (AE): ok that tradeoff seems reasonable for checkout where a few dozen prefixes cover 80% of cases.
[05:31] Priya (Nimbus): can we do canary on dedicated for just checkout? keep recs on hosted?
[05:35] Samir (SE): yes that's the suggested play. canary 5% traffic to dedicated pool for checkout route, monitor p95 and token cost, then expand if stable.
[05:44] Jordan (Nimbus): what telemetry will we see in console to decide "go/no-go" for canary?
[05:49] Samir (SE): console shows per-route p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost per token, cache hit heatmap, and per-node trace events. we'll set an alert for p95 > 350ms or error rate > 0.5%.
[05:59] Priya (Nimbus): excellent. on the pricing side, can you send a simple units-per-dollar sheet we can share with finance?
[06:04] Alex (AE): yes I'll send the simplified pricing deck and a CSV of the sample numbers.
[06:09] Markus (Nimbus): any concerns about data residency? we operate across EU and US and need logs kept in region.
[06:15] Alex (AE): we can pin region and retain logs by region for dedicated and private. hosted has region options too; we'll include retention options in the follow up.
[06:25] Priya (Nimbus): quick tactical: for the next run, please include 2 prompt families we care about plus the cart-peek microbenchmark and post-purchase chat. also include a short tail distribution to catch spikes.
[06:36] Samir (SE): will do. also note we found a small mislabel in the sample where route name "rec-1" became "rec l" in the CSV — auto-transcribe bug, we'll clean up naming.
[06:46] Priya (Nimbus): thanks. anything else on tuning knobs?
[06:50] Samir (SE): two knobs: batch target and prefix cache TTL; third is quantization profile. for checkout we recommend: batch 8, prefix-ttl 60s, 4-bit quant. for recs: batch 12, prefix-ttl 30s, 8-bit to be safer on quality.
[07:06] Jordan (Nimbus): i'm worried about hallucinations with 4-bit on longer completions in rec flows, so 8-bit makes sense there.
[07:12] Alex (AE): agreed. we'll propose the split config in the follow up.
[07:16] Priya (Nimbus): timeline: assuming we get the 10k run CSV by 10/18 and we review results, can we target canary by 10/24?
[07:23] Alex (AE): yes that's feasible for a 5% checkout canary.
[07:27] Markus (Nimbus): must ensure SSO test and audit log checks before the canary.
[07:31] Alex (AE): noted. we'll include security pre-req checklist.
[07:35] Samir (SE): i'll also attach the raw trace events and note any node-level GC.
[07:40] Priya (Nimbus): thanks team. final ask — include a per-route tokens/sec/$ table and a small ROI calc for dedicated vs hosted over 30 days.
[07:51] Alex (AE): will do, i'll include a two-line ROI calc and assumptions.
[07:56] Priya (Nimbus): ok great, thanks everyone.
[07:59] Alex (AE): thanks — recap of next steps now.
